slides.title: Day 1 · The map
slides.body: Your cerebellum sits below and behind the rest of your brain, yet it holds about 80% of your neurons. Counting cells in four adult male brains, Azevedo and colleagues found about 86 billion neurons in total. About 69 billion, or 80%, were in the cerebellum, a wrinkled ball of tissue below and behind the rest of the brain. The cerebral cortex, the brain's large outer layer, held about 16 billion, or 19%. Size and neuron count tell very different stories.

slides.title: Region 1 · Cerebrum and cortex
slides.body: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain. Its gray outer layer is the cerebral cortex. Its frontal lobes help control thinking, planning and problem-solving.

slides.title: Region 2 · Limbic system
slides.body: Deep, paired structures known as the limbic system govern emotions and memories. The hippocampus sends memories to the cerebrum for storage, then retrieves them.

slides.title: Region 3 · Brainstem
slides.body: The brainstem links the brain to the spinal cord. It controls heart rate, blood pressure and breathing.

slides.title: Region 4 · Cerebellum
slides.body: The cerebellum coordinates movement using input from the eyes, ears and muscles. It holds about 69 billion of the brain's 86 billion neurons.

slides.title: Ask which region it targets
slides.body: Every brain drug or device acts somewhere. Ask which region it targets and which job it hopes to change.

slides.title: The rule
slides.body: In neuroscience, start with the map: each region runs different jobs.

keyTerms.definition: The gray outer layer of the cerebrum, the largest part of the brain.
A limbic structure that sends memories off to be stored and later retrieves them.
The part of the brain that links it to the spinal cord and runs vital functions.

items.text: Merging input from eyes and ears

exercises.explanation: The cerebrum thinks and plans, the brainstem keeps you alive, and the cerebellum coordinates movement.

exercises.prompt: Which deep structure sends memories off to be stored and later retrieves them?
exercises.explanation: The hippocampus, part of the limbic system, sends memories to the cerebrum and retrieves them later.

exercises.prompt: What share of the brain's neurons sit in the cerebellum?
exercises.explanation: About 80%: roughly 69 billion of 86 billion. The cortex holds about 19%.
